title: Spiral structures in an embedded protostellar disk driven by envelope accretion
question: Whether spiral structures can appear in the early embedded phase of star formation in a protostellar disk accreting from an infalling envelope, and what mechanism drives them.

what.value: Bolometric temperature of HH 111 VLA 1 (78 K)

evidence.quote: temperature of only 78 K [19], it is a Class I source and therefore young.

what.value: Central star mass M_* ~ 1.5 +/- 0.5 M_sun, envelope mass ~0.6 M_sun, and envelope infall rate ~4.2 x 10^-6 M_sun yr^-1

evidence.quote: The central star has a mass M ∗ ∼ 1.5 ± 0.5M ⊙ [5,20,22] . The infall rate in the envelope towards the [(][20][)] center is estimated at ∼ 4.2 × 10 [−][6] M ⊙ yr [−][1] .
The source is deeply embedded in an envelope with a mass of ∼ 0.6 M ⊙, extending out to ∼ 7000 au from the VLA 1 source [5,20] .

what.value: Previous Cycle 3 ALMA observations of HH 111

evidence.quote: In order to restore a larger size scale, we combined these observations with our previous Cycle 3 observations [23], which had the same correlator setup but a larger MRS of ∼ 1 [′′] . 4.

recipe.goal: Measure size and orientation of HH 111 VLA 2 disklike structure
recipe.method: Gaussian deconvolution of the 343 GHz continuum emission around VLA 2

recipe.goal: Deproject HH 111 VLA 1 disk and isolate non-axisymmetric spiral structures
recipe.method: Rotate disk to align major axis with vertical, estimate inclination from aspect ratio, deproject continuum map by inclination angle, compute annularly averaged map, and subtract annular mean map from deprojected map
key_parameters: Inclination angle of disk axis ~18 deg to the plane of the sky (from aspect ratio ~0.3)

recipe.goal: Extract spiral arm peak positions and fit spiral morphology and pitch angles
recipe.method: Locate emission peak positions of the NE and SW arms by fitting Gaussians by eye to radial intensity cuts every 10 deg in position angle on the difference map, then fit peak positions in polar coordinates (R, theta) with logarithmic and Archimedean spiral models
key_parameters: Radial cuts every 10 deg in position angle
assumptions: Radial error bars taken as width at half maximum of the fitted Gaussians

recipe.goal: Model 343 GHz dust continuum of VLA 1 disk to derive disk mass and Toomre Q stability parameter
recipe.method: Construct axisymmetric parametrized flared disk model with outer thinning, compute LTE radiative transfer integrated along lines of sight tilted by ~18 deg, convolve with telescope beam to fit observed continuum map, and integrate surface density to obtain disk mass and Toomre Q profile
key_parameters: 6 free parameters: R_t, R_o, q, T_t, p, and n_t
Disk axis tilted ~18 deg from plane of sky
assumptions: Vertical hydrostatic equilibrium with Keplerian rotation around M_* ~ 1.5 M_sun, and outer geometric thinning between R_t and R_o
Mass density rho = 1.4 n m_H2 (helium at solar abundance) and gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100
Dust opacity law kappa_nu = 0.1 (nu / 10^12 Hz)^beta cm^2 g^-1 with beta = 0.6 to 1.0, giving kappa_nu ~ 0.054 - 0.035 cm^2 g^-1 at 343 GHz
